---
title: "Live preview"
description: "Use the preview pane to watch local changes during Copilot turns, check the deployed app, switch Fabric shell views, and handle busy preview ports."
---

The preview pane shows your Rayfin app while you build. During a Copilot turn, Fabricator may show a local Vite preview so frontend changes appear as they are made. After the turn finishes, the pane returns to the deployed app.

![The preview toolbar above the running app: back, forward and reload, the Live status with the app’s address, and the Fabric, Design and full-screen buttons.](/screenshots/preview-toolbar.webp)

## What the preview shows

Fabricator uses two preview sources:

1. The local preview, at a `localhost` address, appears while Copilot is working, when the project has Vite installed under `node_modules`. Fabricator starts the project's own local Vite server directly. It does not require an `npm run dev` script.
2. The deployed app shows the rest of the time. After a successful turn, Fabricator redeploys eligible changes and reloads the deployed preview. Its state, such as live, deploying or failed, is on the deployment control in the app bar.

The local preview uses the existing Fabric deployment's `VITE_*` configuration. It does not start a local Fabric backend. If the project has no local Vite installation, Fabricator keeps showing the deployed preview instead.

With **Deploy after each chat turn** off (see [Deploy manually](/docs/ship/deploy#deploy-manually)), the local preview runs whenever the app is open, not only during a turn.

Team app previews are handled by the team pipeline and local preview behavior. See [Work on a team app](/docs/team/work-on-an-app).

## Use the toolbar

The preview toolbar gives you browser-like controls and Fabricator-specific tools:

- **Back**, **Forward** and **Reload** navigate the preview history.
- The address shows what the preview is showing: your deployed app's, or `localhost` for the local preview. Select it to open the page in your default browser.
- For a team app, a status label names the deployment you're looking at, **My preview** or **Published**, and says **Deploying…** while the pipeline updates it. Its local preview is marked **Published data** while it uses the published app's data, and **No data yet** before anything is deployed.
- **Fabric** switches between the direct app view and the app embedded in the Fabric portal shell, when the deployment has a portal link. If the Fabric shell is unavailable, the button is disabled.
- **Design** opens Design mode. On the local preview, it's available only between turns, with **Deploy after each chat turn** off. While a deploy runs, it waits until the deploy ends.
- **Focus** hides the chat and gives the preview more room. **Exit focus** shows the chat again.

When Design mode is on, the extra preview-width buttons are **Desktop**, **Tablet** and **Phone**. **Desktop** fills the pane, **Tablet** previews at 820 CSS pixels, and **Phone** previews at 390 CSS pixels.

> [!NOTE]
> Browser devtools are available from the native preview's webview, not as a separate toolbar button in the current PreviewPane source.

## Zoom and display scale

The preview tracks Fabricator's UI scale and the browser surface's pixel ratio. That matters when you move Fabricator between monitors or change display scaling: the native preview is resized and repositioned to stay aligned with its pane.

In Design mode, device widths account for Fabricator's UI scale, so **Tablet** and **Phone** still represent the app's CSS width instead of the physical monitor width.

## Sign in inside the preview

Signing in to the deployed app is separate from Fabricator's Fabric CLI session. The app preview has its own browser session and cookies. If the app opens a Fabric or Microsoft Entra sign-in popup, Fabricator lets the preview browser handle that popup.

In apps created from the Universal App template, the local preview signs you in automatically when the app uses sign-in. It uses the Fabric account that Fabricator deploys with, so a chat turn doesn't stop at the app's sign-in page. The deployed app doesn't include this and still asks you to sign in. Rayfin describes how it works in [Local automatic sign-in](https://rayfin.ai/docs/start/develop-locally#local-automatic-sign-in).

Older apps need Rayfin 1.36 or newer for this. See [Rayfin versions](/docs/ship/rayfin-versions). To add it to an older app, paste this prompt:

```prompt title="Sign in automatically in the local preview"
Make the local preview sign me in automatically with my Rayfin CLI account. Add @microsoft/rayfin-local-dev at the same version as the app's other Rayfin packages, register rayfinLocalDev({ autoLogin: true }) in vite.config.ts, and set externalEntraExchange: true under services.auth.fabric in rayfin/rayfin.yml. When the app starts in development without a saved session, get the local session token and sign in with signInWithBrokeredToken(). Keep that code behind import.meta.env.DEV with a dynamic import so production builds don't include it.
```

Refreshing Fabricator's Fabric authentication affects Rayfin CLI deployment credentials. It does not sign the preview browser in or out.

## When every preview port is busy

The live local preview must use a `localhost` port your app accepts for sign-in. Fabricator first tries the registered `http://localhost:N` ports from `rayfin/rayfin.yml`. If all registered ports are busy, you see a dialog titled like `localhost:5173 is in use`.

Depending on the situation, the dialog can offer:

1. **Use port N**. Fabricator adds `http://localhost:N` to `rayfin/rayfin.yml`. If the app is already deployed, it also pushes the sign-in setting to Fabric without rebuilding the app.
2. a **Stop node.exe**-style button. Fabricator stops the specific process it identified, then uses the original port. The dialog warns that unsaved work in that process is lost.
3. **Skip live preview**. Fabricator skips the local Vite preview for this turn. You can keep chatting, and the deployed preview takes over after the turn.

If switching ports would require a push while Copilot is already working, the dialog explains that it cannot happen during the turn and asks you to skip for now.

For recovery steps, see [Preview problems](/docs/troubleshooting/preview), especially the "All preview ports are busy" section.
